name: analyze-causal-inference
job: Turn a causal claim into an explicit intervention, estimand, identification argument, and falsifiable analysis.

inScope: Stating the causal question, estimand, and counterfactual contrast
Drawing causal assumptions and choosing an identified design
Running diagnostics, sensitivity, and negative-control checks
Producing a Causal Inference Record with claim boundaries
outOfScope: Product A/B protocol design and event instrumentation (review-domain)
Competing root-cause diagnosis without an estimand (analyze-critically)

inputs: The causal claim and its counterfactual contrast
Experimental or observational data and assignment context
Population, outcome, time zero, and follow-up horizon
outputs: Causal Inference Record: question, causal model, identification and design
Analysis with uncertainty, diagnostics, negative controls, and sensitivity
Claim boundary: supported statements and evidence that would change them

permissions: data access permitted by the owning governance

failureSemantics: Not identified is a valid result when evidence cannot support the causal claim; association, prediction accuracy, or temporal order alone never becomes a causal claim, and unresolved threats stay in the record.

outcome.observable: A Causal Inference Record with an explicit estimand, identification assumptions, diagnostics, uncertainty, and claim boundary that an independent analyst can reproduce from the same data.
